title: Stable-curve automorphisms are faithful on invertible level torsion
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $g\geq2$, and let $C/k$ be a stable unpointed genus-$g$ curve in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], possibly singular or reducible. Let $n\geq3$ be an integer invertible in $k$. Write $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ for the group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O_C$-modules having degree zero on each irreducible component; its group law is tensor product [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)[n]$ be the subgroup of classes $[L]$ with $L^{\otimes n}\simeq\mathcal O_C$. If $a\in\operatorname{Aut}_k(C)$ satisfies $a^*[L]=[L]$ for every $[L]\in\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)[n]$, then $a=\operatorname{id}_C$. No hypothesis that the order of $a$ or the order of $\operatorname{Aut}_k(C)$ is invertible in $k$ is imposed. Degree on a component means degree after pullback to its normalization. Fields and algebraic closure are [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure].

source.place: Lemma 3.5.1 and its proof, printed pp.139--140; the lemma includes singular stable curves and arbitrary characteristic prime to n. Local PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stable-relative-picard-kummer] to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The field base is locally Noetherian and the curve is a stable unpointed genus-$g$ family with $g\geq2$. It gives the smooth separated commutative group algebraic space $N=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ of finite presentation and connected fibres, an extension of an abelian variety by a torus. Its $k$-points are precisely the multidegree-zero line bundle classes in the statement. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, its torus is split. Functoriality for family isomorphisms supplies the group-space automorphism $u=a^*$ of $N$, and its action on $N[n](k)$ is the stated pullback on line bundles. Thus $u(x)=x$ for all $x\in N[n](k)$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.1 proof, printed pp.139–140; uniform finite-free endomorphism-ring version of the torus/abelian congruence argument, using Milne AV I 10.15 and 14.5. Primary PDF read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stable-isom-finite-unramified] to the two families both equal to $C$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The resulting finite unramified automorphism scheme is affine with a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra $B$. Its distinct $k$-points give distinct maximal ideals of $B$; by the Chinese remainder theorem any $m$ such ideals give a quotient $k^m$, hence $m\leq\dim_k B$. Thus the ordinary group $\operatorname{Aut}_k(C)$ is finite. Among its powers of $a$ two agree; cancellation yields $a^r=\operatorname{id}_C$ for an integer $r\geq1$. By the functoriality for family isomorphisms in [lem-sfb-stable-relative-picard-kummer], iterating pullback by this same automorphism gives $u^r=(a^r)^*=(\operatorname{id}_C)^*=\operatorname{id}_N$; contravariance reverses order but does not change powers of a single map. This argument does not require $r$ to be invertible in $k$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.1 proof, printed pp.139–140; uniform finite-free endomorphism-ring version of the torus/abelian congruence argument, using Milne AV I 10.15 and 14.5. Primary PDF read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The semiabelian space $N$ of step 1 satisfies [lem-sfb-semiabelian-hom-finite-free], applied with $G=H=N$. Consequently $R=\operatorname{End}_{k\text{-grp}}(N)$ is a unital associative ring with a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis for its additive group and identity $1_R=\operatorname{id}_N$. In this ring put $f=u-1_R$. It is a group-space homomorphism, and step 1 gives $f(x)=u(x)-x=0$ for every $x\in N[n](k)$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.1 proof, printed pp.139–140; uniform finite-free endomorphism-ring version of the torus/abelian congruence argument, using Milne AV I 10.15 and 14.5. Primary PDF read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-torsion-kernel-divisibility] with $G=H=N$, $f=u-1_R$, and the same $n$. The base field is algebraically closed, $N$ is semiabelian, $n\geq3$ implies $n\geq1$, and $n$ is invertible in $k$; step 3 verifies vanishing on every required torsion point. Obtain $b\in R$ with $u-1_R=n b$, so $u=1_R+n b$.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.1 proof, printed pp.139–140; uniform finite-free endomorphism-ring version of the torus/abelian congruence argument, using Milne AV I 10.15 and 14.5. Primary PDF read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-finite-free-ring-congruence-torsion] for $R,u,b,n,r$. Step 3 verifies the finite $\mathbf Z$-basis hypothesis, step 2 gives $u^r=1_R$ with $r\geq1$, and step 4 gives $u=1_R+n b$ with $n\geq3$. Hence $u=1_R=\operatorname{id}_N$. In particular $a^*[L]=[L]$ for every $[L]\in\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$, without any torsion restriction.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.1 proof, printed pp.139–140; uniform finite-free endomorphism-ring version of the torus/abelian congruence argument, using Milne AV I 10.15 and 14.5. Primary PDF read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Now [lem-sfb-stable-picard-action-faithful] applies to the original $k,C,g,a$: the field is algebraically closed, $g\geq2$, $C$ is stable unpointed, and step 5 establishes identity on every multidegree-zero line bundle class. Its conclusion is $a=\operatorname{id}_C$, as required.

Base status: the item is unsplit in live and side-live with the same statement, now also citing def-weil-algebraic-closure; nothing is weakened. The only citer (lem-sfb-stable-level-versal-branch-freeness, ℓ≥3 prime and invertible) fits the item's hypotheses. No re-split note exists. Against the earlier heads 127e/919d/be34, the only change is in step 2: a CRT bound on the number of k-points of the finite Isom scheme, plus the direct relative-Picard functoriality citation. Both are correct. Steps: (1) relative-picard over Spec k gives a semiabelian N with N(k)=Pic^0(C), split torus, and u=a^*; (2) the Isom scheme over k is finite, so Aut_k(C) is finite, a^r=id and u^r=id, with no condition that r is prime to p; (3) End(N) is finite free with 1=id; (4) divisibility gives u−1=nb; (5) the existing congruence node, whose hypotheses match one for one and which I re-proved via the left regular representation and Milne AV Lemma 14.5 (read locally, p.63), gives u=1; (6) DM 1.13 on all of Pic^0 gives a=id. New nodes: the semiabelian Hom-finite-free node is true (T→A' and A→T' maps vanish, Milne 10.15 read locally) and is not a duplicate, since the existing abelian node needs properness. The semiabelian torsion-divisibility node is true ([n] is finite étale with reduced kernel for invertible n; G_m small case checked) and is a strict generalization of the existing abelian node. The full-Pic^0 faithfulness node has a strictly stronger hypothesis than the item, so it is not a restatement; I tested it on an elliptic tail, two P^1s meeting in three points, and rational components. Deligne Gabber 3.5.1 and DM 1.13 have no local PDFs (WANTED, numdam), so I checked them against the standard statements. n=2 fails (hyperelliptic involution), so n≥3 is necessary. No SGA source. Batch-5: def-trf-algebraic-space and def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism (reached through def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, also from lem-sfb-stable-isom-finite-unramified) are general definitions, and finiteness of Aut of a stable curve is not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so all four flagged citations are accepted. lean.statement: theorem picard_torsion_faithfulness (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (g : ℕ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) (C : Fiber (Spec (.of k)) g 0 (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))))) (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hinv : IsUnit (n : k)) (a : Aut (fiberCurve C)) (hfix : ∀ L : (fiberCurve C).left.Pic, (∀ Z : irreducibleComponents (fiberCurve C).left, @Scheme.Modules.degree k _ (((fiberCurve C).left).reducedNormalizationComponent Z).normalization ⟨((fiberCurve C).left).normalizedComponentMap Z ≫ (fiberCurve C).hom⟩ ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (((fiberCurve C).left).normalizedComponentMap Z)).obj ((fromSkeleton (fiberCurve C).left.Modules).obj L.val)) = 0) → L ^ n = 1 → Scheme.Pic.map a.hom.left L = L) : a = 1
